relations.definition: A corporation discontinuing a product feature
relations.embedding_query_text: retracted: A corporation discontinuing a product feature

chosen_property.label: successorOf
chosen_property.justification: The 'successorOf' property aligns with the definition of a corporation discontinuing a product by indicating a replacement lineage between products.

candidates.label: tocContinuation
candidates.comment: A table of contents continuation relation between a HyperToc entry and the next default HyperToc entry to play or render. Also called next entry, subsequent entry, continued by. Examples: "Chapter 1 tocContinuation 'Chapter 2'", "Segment A tocContinuation 'Segment B'", "HyperTocEntry 'Intro' tocContinuation 'Main Content'".

candidates.label: ownedThrough
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was relinquished. Also called disposal date, date sold, ownership end date. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2023-05-20'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2022-11-30T16:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedThrough '2024-01-01'". Distinct from ownedFrom, which is the date ownership began.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: itemDefectReturnLabelSource
candidates.comment: A return label provision relation between a merchant return policy and the method by which a customer obtains a shipping label for defective product returns. Also called defect return label method, faulty item return label source, return label for defects. Examples: A return policy has itemDefectReturnLabelSource of 'InStore'. A return policy has itemDefectReturnLabelSource of 'PrintAtHome'. A return policy has itemDefectReturnLabelSource of 'DownloadAndPrint'.

candidates.label: customerRemorseReturnFees
candidates.comment: A return policy relation between a merchant return policy and the type of fees applied when a product is returned due to customer remorse. Also called: remorse return fees, change-of-mind return fees, customer-initiated return charges. Examples: "Electronics Store" customer remorse return fees "ReturnShippingFees", "Clothing Retailer" customer remorse return fees "RestockingFee", "Bookstore" customer remorse return fees "NoFees".

candidates.label: isAccessoryOrSparePartFor
candidates.comment: A product compatibility relation between a product and the other products for which it serves as an accessory or spare part. Also called accessory for, spare part for, compatible with, used with. Examples: A phone case isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'iPhone 15'. A replacement battery isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'Laptop Model X'. A camera lens isAccessoryOrSparePartFor 'DSLR Camera Y'. Distinct from isConsumableFor, which refers to items that are used up.

candidates.label: replacee
candidates.comment: A replacee relation between a replace action and the entity that is being substituted. Also called item replaced, old item. Examples: "A replace action involves a replacee 'old battery'.", "A document update replaces 'version 1.0'.", "A software upgrade replaces 'legacy system'.". Distinct from replacer, which is the entity doing the replacing.

candidates.label: dissolutionDate
candidates.comment: A dissolution date relation between an organization and the date when it was dissolved. Also called "closure date", "ceased operations date", "disbandment date". Examples: "Company 'Acme Corp' dissolutionDate '2023-01-15'", "Non-profit organization dissolutionDate '2022-07-01'", "Partnership dissolutionDate '2024-03-10'".

candidates.label: productSupported
candidates.comment: A support relation between a contact point and the product or service it provides support for. Also called supports product, provides support for, related to product. Examples: "Apple Support contact point supports iPhone.", "Microsoft customer service supports Windows.", "Help desk supports enterprise software."

candidates.label: restockingFee
candidates.comment: A charge applied for restocking returned products, specified as a monetary amount or a percentage. Also called return fee, re-shelving charge, return processing fee. Examples: `Standard Return Policy` restockingFee `"$5.00"`, `Seasonal Return Policy` restockingFee `"15% of item price"`, `Electronics Return Policy` restockingFee `"$25"`. Distinct from `returnFees`, which is an enumeration of the *type* of return fees, not the amount.

relations.definition: A corporation applying a technical feature to its products
relations.embedding_query_text: implemented: A corporation applying a technical feature to its products

chosen_property.label: hasTechnicalFeature
chosen_property.definition: A corporation applying a technical feature to its products.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property directly captures a corporation implementing a technical feature, so a new property is minted.

candidates.label: targetProduct
candidates.comment: A compatibility relation between software source code and the software application or operating system it is intended for. Also called "compatible with", "designed for", "applies to product", "software target". Examples: "The source code has targetProduct Windows 10", "The script's targetProduct is Microsoft Excel", "This code is written for targetProduct Linux."

candidates.label: assemblyVersion
candidates.comment: A product or technology version associated with an API reference. Also called: API version, product version, technology version. Examples: "APIReference 'ASP.NET' assemblyVersion '.NET Framework 4.5'", "APIReference 'Java API' assemblyVersion 'Java SE 11'."

candidates.label: legislationEnsuresImplementationOf
candidates.comment: An implementation assurance relation between two pieces of legislation, where one ensures the implementation of the other by modifying national laws. Also called: implements, ensures compliance with, enforces. Examples: "National Law A legislationEnsuresImplementationOf EU Regulation B", "State Statute legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Federal Act", "Local Ordinance legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Regional Directive". Distinct from legislationTransposes, which specifically refers to fulfilling objectives by passing implementation measures.

candidates.label: featureList
candidates.comment: A feature list relation between a software application and the functionalities or modules it provides. Also called: application features, software capabilities, module list. Examples: "Word Processor" feature list "Spell Check, Grammar Check, Document Templates", "Photo Editor" feature list "Layers, Filters, Cropping", "Operating System" feature list "Multitasking, File Management, User Accounts".

candidates.label: accessibilityFeature
candidates.comment: An accessibility feature relation between a creative work and its specific features designed to enhance accessibility. Also called accessible features, accessibility enhancements, content adaptations. Examples: "A movie's accessibility feature is 'captions'.", "An image's accessibility feature is 'altText'.", "A document's accessibility feature is 'highContrast'."

candidates.label: productSupported
candidates.comment: A support relation between a contact point and the product or service it provides support for. Also called supports product, provides support for, related to product. Examples: "Apple Support contact point supports iPhone.", "Microsoft customer service supports Windows.", "Help desk supports enterprise software."

candidates.label: processorRequirements
candidates.comment: A technical attribute detailing the specific processor architecture required to run a software application. Also called CPU requirements, architecture compatibility, processor type. Examples: A software application has processor requirements of 'x86-64'. The program needs processor requirements 'ARM64'. The operating system specifies processor requirements 'IA64'.

candidates.label: model
candidates.comment: A model relation between a product and its product model or textual identifier. Also called: product model, version, type. Examples: "Smartphone model 'iPhone 15 Pro'", "Car model 'Toyota Camry'", "Laptop model 'MacBook Air M2'".

candidates.label: softwareAddOn
candidates.comment: A relation between a software application and an additional software component that extends its functionality. Also called "software extension", "application add-on", "plugin for", "enhances software". Examples: "Photoshop has softwareAddOn a filter pack", "A game's softwareAddOn is a DLC", "This softwareAddOn provides new features for the main application."

candidates.label: serviceOutput
candidates.comment: The tangible item or product that is generated or delivered as a result of a service. Also called service product, service deliverable, output of service. Examples: `Passport Application Service` serviceOutput `Passport`, `Permit Application Service` serviceOutput `Building Permit`, `Printing Service` serviceOutput `Printed Documents`.

relations.definition: A media organization recognizing and documenting an event
relations.embedding_query_text: identified: A media organization recognizing and documenting an event

instances: BBC Verify report -> BBC Verify AI tool misuse test

chosen_property.label: identifies
chosen_property.definition: A media organization recognizing and documenting an event as a misinformation report.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property matches the relation of a report identifying a misinformation report.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: recognizingAuthority
candidates.comment: A recognizing authority relation between a medical entity and the organization that officially endorses it within a system of medicine. Also called endorsed by, officially recognized by. Examples: "A medical treatment is recognized by 'the World Health Organization'.", "A medical specialty is recognized by 'the American Medical Association'.", "A traditional medicine practice is recognized by 'a national health ministry'."

candidates.label: associatedArticle
candidates.comment: A news article linked to a media object. Also called: related article, accompanying article, news story link. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video of Protest' associatedArticle 'NewsArticle on Protest'", "MediaObject 'Photo of Event' associatedArticle 'Article about Event'."

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: broadcastAffiliateOf
candidates.comment: An organization representing the media network(s) whose content is broadcast on a broadcast service. Also called: network affiliation, broadcast network. Examples: "BroadcastService 'Local TV Station' broadcastAffiliateOf 'NBC'", "BroadcastService 'Radio Station' broadcastAffiliateOf 'NPR'."

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

relations.definition: An expert pointing out potential dangers of a technology
relations.embedding_query_text: highlighted_risks: An expert pointing out potential dangers of a technology

instances: Henk van Ess -> Henk van Ess AI risk analysis

chosen_property.label: expertConsiderations
chosen_property.justification: The 'expertConsiderations' property from schema.org is repurposed to link a person to a risk assessment, despite its original domain being Diet.

candidates.label: accessibilityHazard
candidates.comment: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."

candidates.label: risks
candidates.comment: The specific physiological dangers or adverse effects associated with a particular diet plan. Also called diet hazards, health risks of diet, diet side effects. Examples: `Keto Diet` risks `"Nutrient deficiencies"`, `Fad Diet` risks `"Metabolic imbalance"`, `Vegan Diet` risks `"Vitamin B12 deficiency if not supplemented"`.

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: pregnancyWarning
candidates.comment: A medical attribute providing precautions, guidance, or contraindications regarding a drug's use during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy precautions, drug-pregnancy risks, maternal warnings. Examples: A drug has a pregnancy warning 'Consult doctor before use'. The medication includes a pregnancy warning about 'potential fetal harm'. There is a pregnancy warning against 'use in first trimester'.

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

candidates.label: expertConsiderations
candidates.comment: An expert considerations relation between a diet and the medical expert advice pertinent to that dietary plan. Also called: medical advice, professional guidance, health warnings. Examples: "Keto Diet" expert considerations "Consult a doctor if you have kidney issues", "Vegan Diet" expert considerations "Ensure adequate B12 supplementation", "Low-Sodium Diet" expert considerations "Monitor blood pressure regularly".

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: estimatesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk estimation relation between a medical risk estimator and the medical entity whose risk is being assessed. Also called "predicts risk for", "assesses likelihood of", "calculates risk of". Examples: "Medical risk estimator 'Framingham Score' estimatesRiskOf 'Cardiovascular Disease'", "Genetic test estimatesRiskOf 'Type 2 Diabetes'", "Screening tool estimatesRiskOf 'Breast Cancer'".

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

relations.definition: An expert voicing worries about specific applications of technology
relations.embedding_query_text: expressed_concern: An expert voicing worries about specific applications of technology

instances: Henry Ajder -> Henry Ajder conflict zone warning

chosen_property.label: expertConsiderations
chosen_property.justification: The 'expertConsiderations' property is reused to link a person to a risk assessment, even though its original domain is Diet.

candidates.label: expertConsiderations
candidates.comment: An expert considerations relation between a diet and the medical expert advice pertinent to that dietary plan. Also called: medical advice, professional guidance, health warnings. Examples: "Keto Diet" expert considerations "Consult a doctor if you have kidney issues", "Vegan Diet" expert considerations "Ensure adequate B12 supplementation", "Low-Sodium Diet" expert considerations "Monitor blood pressure regularly".

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: processorRequirements
candidates.comment: A technical attribute detailing the specific processor architecture required to run a software application. Also called CPU requirements, architecture compatibility, processor type. Examples: A software application has processor requirements of 'x86-64'. The program needs processor requirements 'ARM64'. The operating system specifies processor requirements 'IA64'.

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: softwareHelp
candidates.comment: A relation between a software application and a creative work providing assistance or guidance for its use. Also called "application help", "software documentation", "user guide for software". Examples: "Microsoft Word has softwareHelp a user manual", "The app's softwareHelp is an online FAQ", "This softwareHelp explains how to use the program."

candidates.label: carrierRequirements
candidates.comment: A description of specific carrier requirements for a mobile application. Also called "network compatibility", "mobile operator requirements", "carrier restrictions". Examples: "Mobile app carrierRequirements 'Requires AT&T network'", "Messaging app carrierRequirements 'Works on all major carriers'".

candidates.label: negativeNotes
candidates.comment: Negative considerations or drawbacks associated with a product or described in a review. Also called cons, disadvantages, downsides, criticisms. Examples: "Product X negativeNotes 'short battery life'", "Review Y negativeNotes 'poor customer service'", "Software Z negativeNotes 'steep learning curve', 'frequent crashes'". Distinct from positiveNotes, which describes favorable aspects.

candidates.label: application
candidates.comment: An application relation between an entry point and the software application capable of fulfilling the associated request. Also called handling application, processing app, execution software. Examples: "A 'view document' entry point's application is 'Adobe Reader'.", "A 'play music' entry point's application is 'Spotify'." Distinct from actionApplication, which is a more specific property for an application that can complete the request.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

relations.definition: A corporation addressing issues raised by a report
relations.embedding_query_text: responded_to: A corporation addressing issues raised by a report

chosen_property.label: correctionsPolicy
chosen_property.justification: The 'correctionsPolicy' property links a corporation to a report, aligning with the definition of addressing issues raised by a report.

candidates.label: diversityStaffingReport
candidates.comment: A diversity staffing report relation between an organization (e.g., news media) and an article or URL containing a report on staffing diversity issues. Also called "staff diversity report", "workforce diversity data", "inclusion metrics report". Examples: "News media organization diversityStaffingReport 'Article on newsroom diversity'", "Company diversityStaffingReport 'URL to annual diversity report'", "Organization diversityStaffingReport 'Self-reported staffing data'".

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: reportNumber
candidates.comment: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."

candidates.label: correctionsPolicy
candidates.comment: A policy relation between an organization and the statement describing its disclosure and correction policy for errors. Also called: error policy, editorial policy, disclosure policy. Examples: "The New York Times" corrections policy "Our commitment to accuracy and transparency...", "Example Corp." corrections policy "Policy on correcting factual errors.", "Academic Journal" corrections policy "Guidelines for authors on submitting corrections.".

candidates.label: acceptedAnswer
candidates.comment: An accepted answer relation between a question and the answer(s) deemed best or most appropriate. Also called best answer, chosen solution, preferred response. Examples: "A forum question's accepted answer is 'Use a screwdriver'.", "A quiz question's accepted answer is 'Option B'."

candidates.label: replyToUrl
candidates.comment: A reply URL relation between user comments and the web address where a response can be submitted. Also called comment reply link, response URL. Examples: "A user comment has a reply to URL 'http://example.com/comment/123/reply'.", "A forum post has a reply to URL 'http://forum.com/thread/456#reply'.", "A blog comment has a reply to URL 'http://blog.com/post/789/comment'."

candidates.label: rsvpResponse
candidates.comment: The specific response (e.g., Yes, No, Maybe) provided to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply. Examples: `Wedding RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Yes`, `Conference RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: No`, `Party Invitation` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Maybe`.

candidates.label: actionableFeedbackPolicy
candidates.comment: An actionable feedback policy relation between a news media organization or organization and a creative work or URL detailing its public engagement and feedback mechanisms. Also called public engagement policy, feedback guidelines, reader interaction policy. Examples: "A news organization's actionable feedback policy is its 'Corrections and Feedback' page.", "The company's actionable feedback policy outlines how customers can submit suggestions."

candidates.label: correction
candidates.comment: A modification relation between a creative work and the comment, text, or document detailing a correction to it. Also called: erratum, amendment, revision, fix. Examples: "News Article" correction "Editor's Note: A previous version of this article misstated...", "Software Manual" correction "See errata sheet for updates.", "Research Paper" correction "Correction published in Vol. 15, Issue 3.".

candidates.label: accessibilityFeature

Also called accessible features, accessibility enhancements, content adaptations. Examples: "A movie's accessibility feature is 'captions'.", "An image's accessibility feature is 'altText'.", "A document's accessibility feature is 'highContrast'."

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: productID

candidates.label: productSupported
candidates.comment: A support relation between a contact point and the product or service it provides support for. Also called supports product, provides support for, related to product. Examples: "Apple Support contact point supports iPhone.", "Microsoft customer service supports Windows.", "Help desk supports enterprise software."

candidates.label: printEdition
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the specific edition of a print product in which a news article is published. Also called edition name, print version, publication edition. Examples: A news article appears in print edition 'Late City Edition'. The story is in print edition 'National Edition'. The article's print edition is 'Weekend Edition'.

candidates.label: softwareAddOn
candidates.comment: A relation between a software application and an additional software component that extends its functionality. Also called "software extension", "application add-on", "plugin for", "enhances software". Examples: "Photoshop has softwareAddOn a filter pack", "A game's softwareAddOn is a DLC", "This softwareAddOn provides new features for the main application."

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: serviceOutput
candidates.comment: The tangible item or product that is generated or delivered as a result of a service. Also called service product, service deliverable, output of service. Examples: `Passport Application Service` serviceOutput `Passport`, `Permit Application Service` serviceOutput `Building Permit`, `Printing Service` serviceOutput `Printed Documents`.

candidates.label: targetProduct
candidates.comment: A compatibility relation between software source code and the software application or operating system it is intended for. Also called "compatible with", "designed for", "applies to product", "software target". Examples: "The source code has targetProduct Windows 10", "The script's targetProduct is Microsoft Excel", "This code is written for targetProduct Linux."

candidates.label: contentType
candidates.comment: A specification relation for an entry point, indicating the supported content type(s) for its response. Also called "response type", "media type", "MIME type". Examples: "API endpoint contentType 'application/json'", "Web page entry point contentType 'text/html'".

chosen_property.justification: The 'includesObject' property is used to link AI content misuse to specific examples (landmark and vehicle).

candidates.label: includedInDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included in data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included in data catalog."

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: includedRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A risk factor inclusion relation between a medical risk estimator and a risk factor used in its calculation. Also called risk factor in calculation, factor considered, included element. Examples: "A medical risk estimator includes a risk factor of age.", "The estimator considers an included risk factor of smoking.", "This tool uses an included risk factor for calculation."

candidates.label: includedComposition
candidates.comment: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.

candidates.label: observationDate
